therapy_note: Marwa is the raag of twilight — the suspended moment between day and night when the light is neither bright nor dark. The near-absence of Sa (the home note) in its actual movement creates a profound sense of restlessness and suspension — the mind wants to resolve but the raag withholds it. This mirrors the emotional state of being between: between a decision, between phases of life, between one state and another. Marwa does not resolve the feeling; it validates it.

bollywood_references.title: Hai Apna Dil Toh Awara
bollywood_references.note: Contains phrases reminiscent of Marwa's restless twilight character — not a strict classical treatment

classical_references.type: Sitar — considered the definitive Marwa recording

notes_for_vocalist: The near-absence of Sa is what makes Marwa so difficult — the home note is there but avoided in movement. Komal Re is the vadi and must be prominent. Ga is SHUDDH (natural, not flat) — this is a common and serious error. Teevra Ma is mandatory; shuddh Ma destroys this raag. Pa is completely forbidden. The overall effect should feel suspended and restless, never arriving home.
common_mistakes: Singing Ga as komal — Marwa has SHUDDH Ga. This is the most common error and completely changes the raag's character.
Using shuddh Ma — only teevra Ma is permitted
Including Pa — it is strictly forbidden
Emphasising Sa too much — Sa is used minimally
variant_notes: Marwa's treatment of Sa varies by gharana — some allow more Sa in development, some restrict it further. Vadi assignment also varies between Re komal and Dha depending on source.
